::: {#sol-boundary}

[Width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 512's best [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) would then be the largest one tried.
A larger rate might do better still,
and the sweep could not say.
When the best value sits at the edge of the range searched,
the range is suspect,
and the next step is to extend it in that direction [@godbole2023playbook].
The actual sweep went one step further, to 3,
where width 512's mean validation [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) drops to `r sprintf("%.3f", py$edge_accuracy_512)`,
about the 0.1 that guessing a digit at random would score.
So the rate that suits width 512 best lies between 0.3 and 3,
and a finer sweep in that range could pin it down.

:::
